description:
Watch a negotiation table long enough and you see it: a man says "Yes, that works for me" — and in the same breath his arms fold across his chest, his chin drops, one foot turns toward the door. Every word says yes. Every line of his body says no.

That gap is what "How to Read a Person Like a Book" by Gerard I. Nierenberg & Henry H. Calero is really about — and it's the opposite of the pop-psych party trick everyone quotes. This is a full summary and analysis of the classic body-language book: gesture clusters, congruence, and why "crossed arms = defensive" is exactly the mistake the authors spent the whole book warning against.

We break down every key idea in plain language — openness, defensiveness, evaluation vs. boredom, suspicion, readiness and control, the lie that touches the nose, frustration held down, and the cluster that matters most: the one you're broadcasting right back. A single gesture is never the sentence.
